Should this be `required` rather than `conditionally_required when available_`
Without `gen_ai.agent.name` the metric becomes a single global histogram and operators won't be able to break latency down by agent.

`gen_ai.tool.name` on the tool metric below is required as the primary dimension. The `invoke_agent` span already carries `gen_ai.agent.name` so I don't see why it would be missing at metric-recording time?

replies.body:
The existing `invoke_agent.client` / `invoke_agent.internal` spans use `conditionally_required: when available` for `gen_ai.agent.name` (see [`spans.yaml#L111-L113`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/model/gen-ai/spans.yaml#L111-L113)) – that's what I was mirroring here.

Would `recommended` work as a compromise? Stronger than the current level, but leaves room for frameworks where the agent has no stable name. Happy to go all the way to `required` if you'd rather.

Same change would apply to #202 and #203.

https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/pull/270 proposes to have an entity for agents so that hosted agents would record their info there instead of recording all agent info on every measurement.

So I think whatever we come up with will change in the future once we add entities/resources into the picture and attribute on the metric itself can't be required. 

For now, I think it makes sense to keep it consistent with internal agent span that (for some unknown to me reason) has `conditionally_required: When available` level
Sounds good — kept as `conditionally_required: When available.` (matching the internal `invoke_agent` span). Also fixed the capitalization per #245.

Looked into this and the scenario tooling doesn't persist metrics to `scenarios/*/data.json` today — the writer in [`reference/src/semconv_genai/data_files.py`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/reference/src/semconv_genai/data_files.py) only emits `spans` and `events` keys (no `metrics`), and none of the existing `data.json` files include a `metrics` section. The parser collects metric signals in-memory but they're never written out. The repo README also has no Metrics report table.

The existing `google-adk` scenario pins ADK v1.34.1, which already emits all 5 of the proposed metrics, so the SDK side is ready — but the conformance pipeline needs to learn about metrics first.

Or am I missing something — is there a way to wire up metric validation that I haven't spotted? Either way, happy to do the work; just want to make sure we're aligned on the approach.

replies.body:
Holding off on adding `gen_ai.provider.name` / `gen_ai.request.model` here for now — the original use case behind this metric is a single-model agent where those dimensions don't add much (`provider` and `model` are already captured on the child `gen_ai.inference` span, and on `gen_ai.client.operation.duration` for any LLM-call-level slicing). Adding them on the agent metric would also double-count cardinality if dashboards also slice the LLM-call metric.

Happy to revisit if there's a concrete use case where slicing agent-level duration by provider/model is useful that I'm missing.

replies.body: Added `gen_ai.agent.id`, `gen_ai.agent.version`, and `gen_ai.request.model` (all `conditionally_required: When/If available.`). Skipped `gen_ai.agent.description` since it tends to be free-form text and risks high cardinality on a metric.

Quick follow-up on this: ended up dropping `gen_ai.agent.version` and `gen_ai.request.model` again on a second look. Kept `gen_ai.agent.id`.

- `gen_ai.agent.version`: the intent in this metric set is to use the `service.version` resource attribute (which is stable, applied process-wide via the resource) for agent/tool/app versioning, rather than carrying a per-signal `gen_ai.agent.version` dimension on every metric. The registry attribute itself stays (it was added by @trask in a separate PR), it just isn't a dimension on this metric.
- `gen_ai.request.model`: not always available at the time this metric is recorded. The framework knows the agent it's invoking, but the model selection can happen later inside the agent (and may differ across the multiple LLM calls within one invocation). The model breakdown is already on the child `gen_ai.inference` / `gen_ai.client.operation.duration` signals; adding it here would conflate two different boundaries.

Happy to revisit either if there's a concrete use case I'm missing.

I believe agent version != service version for remote agents and even when you're hosting an agent the version of agent is NOT the version user sees - you can update your service without incrementing agent version because nothing has changed in user-related agent config or behavior.

For the  request model, we can document that it's the model provided when agent was created. Given that pretty much all frameworks take it as constructor parameter, it seems to be common and important use case.

They can both be `recommended: When available and meaningful / provide information not captured service.version / etc`

Update: added `gen_ai.agent.version` back. Still skeptical about `gen_ai.request.model` though — the multi-model agent case (planner picks executor, "thinking" model delegates to "doing" model, etc.) isn't well covered: the framework would have to pick one value (configured primary? first call? last call?) and different frameworks would pick differently. Happy to add it if there's a clear single-model convention you'd like to land on.

We can clarify that this is the model provided when creating the agent and should be provided if and only if specific framework has this construction-time parameter. It should not be populated when not applicable or when multiple models can be configured on the same agent. The motivation to include it is consistency between spans and metric. Invoke agent internal spans has request model, it's low cardinality and common parameter on existing agent frmaeowrks, so metric should have it too. 

This would be recommended attribute (with note clarifying when to record it) and ADK does not have to populate it. I don't think this PR is blocked on it, but if we merge it as is, I'll send a follow up to clarify and add request model name with these caveats .
